chunks: Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who encounters a wild beast, and salat has become due, but he cannot walk for fear of the lion. He said:
He should face the lion and perform salat, gesturing with his head by way of indication while he is standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the qiblah.

key_terms.السَّبُعُ: a wild beast or predator encountered by the person
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory prayer whose time has arrived
key_terms.الْأَسَدِ: the lion as the immediate danger in the scenario
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer, which is set aside here due to necessity
key_terms.بِرَأْسِهِ: with his head, indicating the modified prayer movement
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: he performs the prayer in the manner he is able
key_terms.يُومِئُ: he gestures instead of performing full bodily motions

ai.seo_question: How should a person perform salat if a lion or wild beast prevents him from facing the qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for salat in a state of danger when a person is unable to move because of fear from a lion or wild beast. It indicates that preserving oneself from immediate harm takes precedence, and the prayer is performed in the possible manner by facing the threat and signaling with the head while standing, even away from the qiblah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1337 - Sama'a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who encounters a wild beast, and the time for prayer has arrived, but he cannot walk due to fear of the lion.
Imam (as) said: "
He should face the lion and perform the prayer, gesturing with his head while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the Qibla."
